answer: In an agent marketplace, tundra buys forecasts from atlas and willow only after each seller locks a separate bond. A seller's total voting weight is proportional to its bonded funds, so splitting one bond among a thousand identities creates no extra influence. Bonds stay locked through a dispute window, and a cryptographic proof of a double vote burns the offender's bond. An attacker must therefore tie up real capital to gain weight and risks losing it by cheating.
